versions.short: The bill would set a policy to limit espionage and foreign influence operations in the Arctic and in United States waters, mainly by foreign adversaries such as China and Russia. It would require foreign vessels to get prior government consent before conducting marine scientific research in United States waters, and would bar the Secretary of State from approving such requests for vessels linked to foreign adversaries, unless a national interest waiver is issued. The bill would also require the Secretary of State, with intelligence and homeland security agencies, to produce within 180 days a strategy to identify and combat foreign espionage in the Arctic, and to report to Congress on related activities and on the review process for research requests. The bill would further require a report to Congress within one year on espionage and influence operations in the Arctic and United States waters, including possible information-sharing among allied Arctic countries.
